Java Interop

The Nabu compiler provides Java interoperability out of the box. Java 20 is supported, and Nabu and Java sources can be mixed in a single project.

What works

  • Nabu can call Java code and Java can call Nabu code.
  • Java and Nabu sources can be mixed in one project.
  • The compiler reads Java class files, including generics and modules, through its resolve/asm package (ASM 9.8). It runs against the class library of the JDK it runs on; JDK 25 is verified.
  • Java sources (up to Java 20) are parsed with the ANTLR Java20Parser.g4 grammar and the JavaCompilerVisitor, and compiled by Nabu.

How Java sources are compiled

Nabu compiles Java sources itself, together with the Nabu sources, with whichever backend is selected. A .java file in a source directory of the Maven plugin is parsed, resolved and compiled like a .nabu file, so Java and Nabu classes can refer to each other freely.

This works for substantial real-world code: the picocli example compiles picocli’s single 19,000-line source file with Nabu, for the JVM and natively, and the result behaves like the official picocli jar.

If the maven-compiler-plugin also runs, javac compiles the Java sources a second time. That can be useful in an existing project that relies on javac; place the nabu-maven-plugin before the maven-compiler-plugin, so the Nabu classes exist when javac runs (see Maven Plugin). To let Nabu compile everything on its own, disable javac for the main sources with <skipMain>true</skipMain>, as the picocli example does.

Reference language level

The reference language level for the frontend is Java 20 (JLS SE 20). Interop and mixed input languages support both Nabu and Java 20 features.
